title: Air-fryer Cumberland sausages
subtitle: The coiled Cumberland sausage cooked in the air fryer until evenly browned.
excerpt: A Cumberland sausage ring cooked in the air fryer until the skin is browned all over and the meat is cooked through, without the need to turn the grill or stand over a frying pan. Serves two.
sourceNotes: Cumberland sausage originates from Cumbria in the north of England and is traditionally coiled into a ring rather than linked. It is a coarsely ground pork sausage with a high meat content, seasoned with black pepper.

content.text: Cumberland sausage in the air fryer produces an evenly browned skin without splitting. The coil shape sits flat in the basket, so the heat reaches all sides. Cook at 180°C rather than higher: the sausage skin splits easily above 190°C before the centre is cooked through.

items.prepNote: Cumberland sausage ring, or 4 thick pork sausages

content.text: Spray the air fryer basket lightly with cooking oil. Place the {{sausages-pork}} sausages in the basket ,  the Cumberland coil flat, link sausages spaced apart. Cook at 180°C for 9 minutes, turn, and cook for a further 7-9 minutes until browned all over and cooked through with no pink visible when cut. Rest for 2 minutes.

items.fix: Cook at 180°C, not 200°C. The skin needs time to cook slowly before the interior pressure builds.

items.cause: Sausage resting against the basket wall.
items.fix: Leave space between sausages so hot air circulates around the whole surface.
A thick Cumberland ring needs the full 18 minutes. Cut into the thickest part to check: no pink, juices run clear.

content.text: Cumberland sausage from the air fryer is good with mash and onion gravy, or with fried eggs and toast for a weekend breakfast. The skin stays intact and the sausage is easy to slice into rounds. The same method works for any thick pork sausage.
